M14.0.SPEC (#419) — toml completeness classification. Every public NAMED node type of the pinned wasm/tree-sitter-toml.wasm is in exactly one bucket. The grammar exposes 20 nodeTypeForId slots but only 19 DISTINCT names: `escape_sequence` is declared twice, which is a grammar quirk rather than two node types. MEASURED, not restated (2026-10-09, commit 840bffea9): enumerating wasm/tree-sitter-toml.wasm through web-tree-sitter's Language API gives 66 node-type slots, of which 20 are NAMED and 19 are distinct named names — exactly the claim above, with the anonymous punctuation tokens making up the remaining 46 slots (44 distinct). ERROR and MISSING are injected by this gate for EVERY language because the wasm ABI does not list them; neither occurs for this grammar and both are silent here. Silence is guilt: a type in no bucket fails section A, and a type the wasm no longer produces is a stale row and also fails. That rule bites hardest on the four DATETIME types — none appears anywhere in cargo's 684 files, so their handling is pinned by FIXTURE rather than by the corpus, and a corpus-only lane would have classified them by assumption and called it coverage. SECTION D IS RED AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE. The gate requires >=2 distinct `evidenceClass` values and TOML has exactly ONE: every edge it emits is `structural`. YAML, the closest config-format precedent, pins four and legitimately so — a merge key is an inference, an anchor is a reference, an `!include` is a fetch. TOML has none of those constructs: no merge, no anchor, no alias, no include, no import, no reference of any kind. Its whole graph is a nesting the document literally writes. Both routes to a second tier are dishonest and neither was taken: emitting a `uses` edge for a path-shaped string imports ecosystem knowledge about which keys are paths in which tool into a format that defines no references, and tagging an edge to an IMPLIED parent as `inferred` points at a target that is deliberately not a symbol, where an edge to a non-existent node is the unresolvable-identity defect. D stays red until the gate grows a documented single-tier allowance or TOML grows a construct that earns one. E and F are the canonical F5 ceremony, exactly as for html.

handled_verified.note: Twenty-one types, each read in src/ast/real-toml-analyzer.ts and each pinned. `ERROR` is handled for the corpus reason recorded on the internal_silent side, and the analyzer now walks for recovery nodes itself — REPORTED at the node's OWN span, BYPASSED, and everything AROUND it still published. It had been pushing no diagnostics at all, so the "reported" half of the contract was entirely the engine's: a contract resting on a caller is not a contract, which is the same blindness the svelte lane had in the opposite direction. `children`, not `namedChild`, because the expected token of a MISSING node can be anonymous. Pinned by `toml/malformed-and-rejected` and `toml/error-node-becomes-symbol`. DECLARED CONSEQUENCE OF THE BYPASS, measured rather than assumed: a key whose VALUE fails to parse is not published. The whole `key = invalid-value` pair sits inside the ERROR, and the walk does not descend into one, so `invalid-section.key` is absent from a document whose table and every earlier key are present. Measured over the whole pool this costs exactly TWO symbols in TWO files, both cargo's own invalid-manifest fixtures. It is declared rather than repaired because recovering the key means inferring table scope from POSITION inside a region the parser marked unreadable — the ERROR sits at document level, so ownership would have to come from "the last header before this offset", and a wrong guess attaches a real key to the wrong table. Two symbols in two intentionally-broken files does not justify that risk, and the alternative is not silence: the file is reported with a parse error at the key's own line. DECLARED, ZERO CORPUS OCCURRENCES: an unterminated header such as `[bad` is recovered by the grammar into a real `table` node whose header children include an ERROR, and a following genuine header is nested inside that ERROR. Read naively the analyzer would publish the invented table and lose the real one. Measured across all 743 files this shape occurs ZERO times, so no behaviour is changed on the strength of a synthetic input — the same discipline that removed the values-as-symbols mutant rather than fixing it, on the grounds that the measured enter state is stronger evidence than a stand-in. It is recorded so a future corpus that does contain the shape inherits the decision instead of rediscovering it.

internal_silent.note: MISSING and `comment` are two types that correctly emit nothing and need no analyzer read. `comment` is a literal: a comment is not an identity, and TOML has no block-comment form, so a `#` line contributes nothing to the graph. MISSING holds across the whole 743-file pool — zero MISSING nodes, and it is a property of this grammar that a recovery node is always a full ERROR rather than an inserted token. ERROR WAS HERE AND WAS WRONG, and the correction is recorded because the reasoning that put it here is the exact trap the svelte lane fell into on the same day. This note previously read "NEITHER OCCURS for this grammar", on the evidence of TWELVE HAND-MADE MALFORMED DOCUMENTS. The corpus was never measured. Measuring it: 2 of 743 files (0.27%) carry an ERROR node — `cargo/tests/testsuite/cargo_add/invalid_manifest/{in,out}/Cargo.toml`, cargo's own deliberately-invalid manifest fixtures, where `key = invalid-value` is a bare word where TOML requires a value. Two hand-made malformed documents and 743 real ones disagreed, and the real ones were right. ERROR now sits in handled_verified, and the analyzer reports it itself rather than leaving the whole contract to the engine.

FALSIFIER, RUN: a `[lints] workspace = true` site becomes resolvable the moment some file declares the symbol `<rootModule>.workspace.lints`; 0 of 84 do, and the two ways to close it (a multi-target edge per declared `[workspace.lints.*]` sub-table, or a fabricated container symbol) are design rulings, not lane fixes. AND THE PREVIOUS INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG ABOUT 124 SITES: it read `[table] -> bare keys` and so called `hasura-engine/v3`'s members unresolvable, while the root declares them as DOTTED KEYS under `[workspace]` (`package.version = "3.0.0"`) and the analyzer publishes `workspace.package.version` for exactly that line. The target existed while the reader said it did not — which is why the split prints both columns

The `[path-bases]` rule (A3) fires on NONE of the 10, which is the control that says the fix took exactly what it could

decisions.question: Should the analyzer decode a quoted key's escapes by WALKING its `escape_sequence` child nodes, or by decoding the quoted_key's own text in pure-String?
decisions.ruling: RULED: decode the PARENT'S TEXT, in pure-String, and never walk `escape_sequence`. The two are equivalent by construction — an escape_sequence node's text is exactly the escape sequence its parent contains — so walking the children would buy nothing and cost a second pass over every quoted key. It would also put the lane's no-regex rule under pressure: the natural way to express a decode is a replacement pattern, and that rule exists because every regex literal is one more thing to audit for backtracking. The decode handles the escapes TOML defines in a key (\n, \t, \r, \", \\, \uXXXX) and passes an UNKNOWN escape through with its backslash rather than dropping it, because silently discarding half a key would invent a different identity. Measured: `"a\u0062c"` resolves to the single key `abc`, and a literal-string key takes a pure slice because a literal string has no escapes at all.
decisions.consequence: `escape_sequence` is classified HERE rather than as handled, so the type is accounted for exactly once and the reason it is not walked is on the record rather than being invisible.

coverage._from: DERIVATION. implemented = the three types the production path fires over the WHOLE admitted population (construct-census, commit 840bffea9; raw run validation/m14/fixtures/toml/tools/census-whole-corpus.json): contains 25,033 edges / 1,474 files, imports 331 / 153, references 167 / 5. The 120-file firing log reads only `contains:882 imports:16` and marks references SILENT — a stride sample that invents an absence — so this block follows the census, not the sample. The six exclusions are grammar-absence, each carrying a count: 0 of the 19 named node types of the pinned grammar (66 node-type slots, 20 named slots, 1 duplicate named slot) can carry the construct, and the corpus corroborates with 0 occurrences or 0 referents. `exports` is deliberately NOT excluded: the lane's own applicability audit (self-test 14/14, positive control fired 167/167 aliases) reports it UNVERIFIED and exits 1 — 174 publish-shaped key sites exist (118 string-valued: module, publish, main, public, exposed), and nothing in this lane MEASURES that TOML cannot express the relation, so it stays IN the denominator as an unimplemented applicable type (a gap) rather than being promoted to grammar-absence. ARITHMETIC: 3 implemented + 0 corpus-unexercised + 1 gap (exports) = 4 applicable = 10 − 6 grammar-absence − 0 unclassified. RELATED ITEM, NOW IMPLEMENTED: TOML-G1 — the workspace-inheritance half of `references` was 1,269 sites in 138 documents and is now 1,183 emitted (all resolving) + 86 measured-residual sites; see the TOML-G1 entry. The `references` edge count is 1,350, not 167, and `_implemented_measured.references` carries the revision. AND `exports` STAYS IN THE DENOMINATOR, with its size re-measured 2026-10-13 over the same 1,485-file population (validation/m14/fixtures/toml/tools/residual-whole-population.mts --exports): 174 publish-surface key sites, 118 string-valued, 0 whose value names a declaration in the SAME document (the census's `referentSites`, reproduced by an independent walk), 1 whose value names a declaration ANYWHERE in the project (`docs/netlify.toml publish = "build"` — a name coincidence, not a publication), and 0 values ending in `.toml`. The lane's admitted population is `.toml` alone, so a file claim cannot verify such a target and a bare-target external claim is unfalsifiable (HANDOFF §5l); the completion score therefore remains 3 of 4 applicable types, not 3/3. AND THE json/toml `exports` CONTRADICTION IS NOW MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and is recorded as an OWNER ADJUDICATION (validation/m14/verification/FOUR-CLAUSE-toml.md §3.2): json's `exports` target is the entry point's OWN KEY SYMBOL declared in the same document — measured, 29 of 29 edges over a 12-document sample through the production path — while toml's 174 sites are CONFIGURATION FIELDS whose VALUE names an artifact (netlify's `publish = "build"` is an output directory; Gradle's `module = "group:artifact"` is a coordinate). The two lanes were not answering the same question; the disposition was left to the owner rather than silently aligned with json's. THE OWNER RULED ON 2026-10-13 (validation/m14/verification/FOUR-CLAUSE-toml.md, LEAD RULING section): the 174 publish-surface sites are a REAL DEFECT — `exports` means a NAME THE UNIT PUBLISHES FOR OTHERS TO IMPORT, and a manifest key whose value is a path/directory/coordinate is a publish-surface fact about an ARTIFACT — so the fix is ANALYZER work and NOT a reclassification, because reclassifying would relabel the number without touching the graph. IMPLEMENTED at the emission site: the eleven conventional leaves generate CANDIDATES, and a candidate becomes an edge ONLY when its value names a declaration of the same document and that declaration is not the site's own context. MEASURED over the whole admitted population: 31 analyzer-visible candidates (the census's 174 also counts 143 pairs nested inside INLINE TABLES, which this lane deliberately does not publish as symbols — see the inline-table ruling in src/ast/real-toml-analyzer.ts), and 0 edges. The one site that passed a weaker test — `docs/netlify.toml`'s `[build] publish = "build"`, the OUTPUT DIRECTORY sharing its enclosing table's name — is now pinned as a fixture negative, and with both guards removed the mutant reads `exports 20 edges · 0 resolved · 1 amb · 19 unresolved · residual 30`, which is the ruled defect measured rather than argued. THE COVERAGE BLOCK IS UNCHANGED: `exports` stays in the denominator as an unimplemented applicable type, so the score stays 3 of 4 — the owner refused the re-wording route to 4/4, and the classification question (gap vs zero-sites) is theirs on this measurement.
